sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: The aim of this document is to describe the web service JI Contract in terms of “what is it” and “how to use it”. It describes the webservice data-model, supported operation and related behavior and available interfaces.
Before going deeper with specific features of this webservice please ensure to review the document “JINT WS Development_Kit – Web Services Overview” which applies to all webservices
The structure of the current document is the following:
1. ImportSpend:

2. Request data format [ImportSpend]: describes the possible operations on import and describes the structure of the request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory depending on the operation you want to perform and those that can be omitted.
3. Behavior [ImportSpend]: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some particular processes.
4. Response Data Format [ImportSpend]: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes.
5. Import:
6. Request data format [Import]: describes the structure of the import request.
7. Behavior [Import]: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some processes
8. Response data format [Import]: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes
9. Export:
10. Component filters [Export]: describes which sections of a contract can be exported. The use of a component filter increments the number of sections in the response to every contract exported.

11. Condition filters [Export]: describes which fields can be used to filter the contract to be extracted on specific conditions. So, the use of a condition filter allows to decrease the number of contract extracted.
12. Export data format [Export]: describes the structure of the response in terms of exported fields and sections.
13. Error codes [Export]: contains a list of possible error codes
14. Validate:

15. Request data format [Validate]: describes the structure of the validation request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory and those that can be omitted.
16. Behavior [Validate]: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input
17. Response Data Format [Validate]: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes
18. SOAP INTERFACE
19. Available methods: contains the list of the methods provided by the web service.
20. WSDL: in this paragraph is attached the JIContract.wsdl from which the web service has been created and is to be used to generate the client.
21. Endpoints: available webservice SOAP endpoint URLs
22. Request samples: sample SOAP requests to invoke the webservice
23. REST INTERFACE:
24. Endpoint definition: describes REST available collections. Allowed calls with allowed parameters and supported HTTP methods
25. Request samples: contains detailed samples of HTTP request/response for each available operation

26. Data Types and UI Default Labels: describes the type of the fields and the corresponding label in English language in the platform with the aim to simplify the mapping between the fields visible in the platform and the fields used in the web service.

paragraphs: Values in the PRSpend field for subsequent updates are added to the current PRSpend total for the contract. For example, if the current PRSpend value for the contract in JI is 1,000.00, and the import document contains a value of [importo], the updated value for the contract in JI, after the import, will be [importo].

sections.title: Import
paragraphs: Contract import method allows creating new contracts and updating existing contracts only. The process does not support deleting contracts.
The contract import document includes header data. You can also include contract custom fields in the document
It is not possible to use contract import to change the contract number. If you provide a new contract number, the CLM solution creates a new contract with that number.
Also, you cannot use contract import to change the currency.

sections.title: Condition filters [Export]
paragraphs: Here are defined extraction condition filters, i.e. the rule to be used for data filtering.
A same condition filter can be expressed more than once. All specified filters are requested to be matched (they are all applied in AND clause).
For instance, it is possible to apply the following filters:
The result will be that all requisition having creation date greater than 2011-11-20 AND lower than 2012-01-20 (between 2011-11-20 AND 2012-01-20) will be retrieved.
Condition filters are also available server side as restrictive conditions. The filter conditions entered client side will be joined with the filter conditions configured server side.

It is possible to enable the component filters according to particular values of the condition filters server side. By this way, it is possible to configure different chains, everyone with different restrictive conditions and therefore with different subsets of component filters enabled.

For instance, based on the specific configuration set up for the single integration, will be possible to allow the webservice client to export only awarded auctions, even if this filter is not set by the integration client.

sections.title: Validate
paragraphs: JI Contract validate method allows to specify the validity of a contract based on its content.
It can also be used to update one or more contract custom fields.

sections.title: Request data format [Validate]
paragraphs: Following table shows the structure of the validate request to submit.

rows: Internal identifier of the contract on which operation is to be executed

Status of the workflow step for the contract.
It can assume following value:
approve – The workflow step is approved. The contract can advance to the next step in the workflow.
approveWithException – The workflow step is approved, but with one or more exceptions. The exceptions should be noted in the Note element. The contract can advance to the next step in the workflow.
return – The workflow step is not approved. The contract is returned to draft status and does not advance to the next step in the workflow.
